newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coalition agrees on 1997 budget savings.
newsitem.headline: German coalition agrees on 1997 budget savings.

text.p: Leaders of Germany's ruling coalition agreed to final spending cuts for the 1997 budget at a meeting on Sunday night, chancellory minister Friedrich Bohl told reporters early on Monday.
Bohl said Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition had agreed to reduce spending by three billion marks. The final budget draft was expected to be rubber-stamped by the three coalition parties on Monday.

The savings met Finance Minister Theo Waigel's calls for cuts to ensure Germany meets the strict budget deficit limit of three percent of gross domestic product next year to qualify for European monetary union.
One billion marks will be cut from the Federal Labour Office budget and another two billion marks in savings will come from across-the-board reductions, Bohl said.
Bohl also said coalition leaders agreed to hold separate discussions from the budget talks in December on making a firm order for the Eurofighter combat aircraft.
